note: The raw fuzzer input is parsed as a serialized SPIX image; this candidate encodes an image that reaches barcode width extraction with height below the 51-scan averaging window.
The SPIX header supplies the image width used later as the number of averaged output samples.
The SPIX header supplies a short image height, smaller than the fixed nscans value used by barcode crossing extraction.
The decoded PIX is passed to the barcode processor using the width-based path.
An 8 bpp image without a colormap is cloned for barcode extraction, preserving its dimensions and raster data.
Detected barcode-like regions are deskewed and clipped into 8 bpp barcode images later analyzed for widths.
The width decoder requests crossing positions for the cropped barcode image.
Crossing extraction always asks for 51 raster scans regardless of the cropped image height.
The branch condition is backwards for short images; when h is less than 51 it enters the else branch instead of clamping nscans to the available image height.
With h < nscans, first becomes negative, so subsequent row iteration starts before the image raster.
The negative i value is used to derive a line pointer before the allocated PIX data.
The byte load through the invalid line pointer reads outside the live raster allocation, matching the reported ASAN read in pixAverageRasterScans.
